description: Ahlfors and Grunsky conjectured that the hexagonal lattice (triangular tiling) yields the extremal configuration for Bloch's constant. Baernstein and Vinson proved local minimality: among ramified coverings branched only over lattice points, the hexagonal lattice is locally optimal. This connects to circle packing, crystallography, and the broader question of which lattice structures optimize covering problems.
mathematical_formalization: The Ahlfors-Grunsky function f_{AG}: D -> C covers C \ Lambda where Lambda = omega_1 Z + omega_2 Z is the hexagonal lattice with omega_1/omega_2 = e^{i*pi/3}. Conjectured: B = B_{f_{AG}} = 1/sqrt(1+sqrt(3)) * Gamma(1/3)*Gamma(11/12)/Gamma(1/4) ~ 0.4719. Baernstein-Vinson: d^2/dt^2 B_{f_t}|_{t=0} >= 0 for variations within the lattice class.
analogical_connections: Hexagonal packing optimality ~ honeycomb conjecture (Hales' theorem)
Lattice covering ~ error-correcting codes and sphere packing
Local minimality ~ stability of crystal structures
Ramified covering variations ~ perturbation theory in quantum mechanics
implementation_hypothesis: Implement the Ahlfors-Grunsky function using the Weierstrass P-function and its inverse. Compute B_{f_AG} to high precision. Then systematically perturb lattice parameters (ratio omega_1/omega_2, branch point positions) and compute B_f for perturbed coverings. Verify local minimality numerically and attempt to extend Baernstein-Vinson's result to larger variation classes.
experiment_seed: Compute B_{f_AG} using elliptic function arithmetic to 50+ digits. Perturb the lattice ratio tau = omega_1/omega_2 in a neighborhood of e^{i*pi/3} and compute B_f(tau). Plot B_f as a function of tau. Verify the local minimum. Test non-lattice branch point configurations.
